title: The alternating sum of a constant over a non-empty masked ground set vanishes
statement: For any constant c, any Bool-valued mask P, any width n and any index i below n at which the mask holds, the even and odd halves of the mask-restricted graded subset sum of the constant summand are EQUAL. In Nat's graded form -- no negatives, so a signed sum lands as a pair (even, odd) and identities are stated as equalities rather than as vanishing differences -- this is the identity Moebius inversion turns on: it is the shape of sum over d dividing n of mu(d) = 0 for n > 1, once the divisor-to-selection transfer exists. Nat.Subsets.sumSel_const is the special case at the full mask, where the witness is free because the top index always qualifies.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Subsets.sumSelOn_const_of_mem : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat.lt x3 x2) -> ((x5 : Eq.{1} Bool (x1 x3) Bool.true) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.Subsets.sumSelOn x1 x2 (fun (x6 : ((x6 : AxNat) -> Bool)) => x0) Bool.true) (AxNat.Subsets.sumSelOn x1 x2 (fun (x6 : ((x6 : AxNat) -> Bool)) => x0) Bool.false)))))))

evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- Nat.Subsets.sumSelOn_const_of_mem 2>/dev/null | grep -Fc '((x4 : AxNat.lt x3 x2) -> ((x5 : Eq.{1} Bool (x1 x3) Bool.true) ->')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pattern is BOTH hypotheses as rendered by Kernel::render_lean, so a statement that dropped either fails this check -- and both are load-bearing, since the conclusion is FALSE without a masked index below the width. The two branches of the induction step are asymmetric: with the top index masked, add_comm closes it and the induction hypothesis is never used; without it, the witness must move below the top index, which needs i /= j, and that comes from the mask itself. So the case split is over the EQUATION P j = false, not Bool.rec on P j -- a Bool.rec branch does not hand you the equation it split on and the contradiction is unreachable inside it.

evidence.supports: NECESSITY of the hypotheses: at the empty mask the conclusion is FALSE, and at a mask whose only index is at or above the width it is also false.
evidence.notes: At the empty mask the fold visits only the empty set, which is EVEN, so the even half is 4 and the odd half is 0. Dropping the hypothesis makes the theorem false, not merely weaker -- the same shape as sum over d dividing n of mu(d) = 0 failing at n = 1, where the only divisor is 1 and it sits entirely on the even side. The second half of that test pins Lt i n separately, with the masked index moved to 5 and the width left at 3.
